# `start_record_avi`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start recording the live view to a video file, optionally as a timelapse.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xdfcb0, StartWriteAvi @0x2eb8f0, EnableWriteAviThr @0x2ee3f0 (64-bit build) |

Updates the recording settings, then starts the recording worker and replies with integer result 0 once the worker exists. Settings can change even if the start fails; there is no rollback. Needs the live image thread running and no planet stack active. Recording format 0 (wide camera, or raw false) writes an MP4 from the processed YUV stream; formats 1 (raw omitted) and 2 (raw true) write a raw-frame AVI; how 2 differs from 1 is unresolved. Depending on process and view mode the request may first be relayed to a secondary unit (wait up to 10000 ms for its occupancy check). Progress comes from AviRecord events: a start event with numeric fps, a fail event with code 218 on file creation failure, and worker state events with timelapse (enable, delay_sec, src_dura_min), saved_frames, raw, file_saved and, when saved, duration_sec and optional name; their full presence rules are unresolved.

Side effects: Copies and overrides the live-view recording settings, may persist the timelapse config, applies the settings, enables the write thread and creates image/video files under the works directory with time-derived names. Shell, storage and setup can add unbounded time.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"start_record_avi"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Optional object. Absent, null, scalar or array params produce an empty map and the defaults apply; arrays are not positional. [READ] |
| `params.raw` | any | no | - | Optional boolean or integer (nonzero is true); a wrong type is ignored. When parsed: on the wide camera it forces recording format 0, on other cameras false gives format 0 and true gives format 2. When missing or unparseable the recording format is 1, so omitting raw differs from raw false (a client MUST NOT assume they are equal). Format 0 records an MP4 from the camera's processed (YUV) stream; formats 1 and 2 both record a raw-frame 8-bit AVI (-RAW.avi name) (READ). How 2 differs from 1 is unresolved: no format-2 branch was found in the writer path. The chosen format is persisted as the rtmp rec_format setting. [READ] |
| `params.timelapse` | object | no | - | Optional object; a missing or wrong-typed value is ignored, as are wrong-typed members (the default stays, no error). A successfully parsed delay_sec or src_dura_min saves the timelapse recording config for the current view mode; enable alone does not. [READ] |
| `params.timelapse.enable` | any | no | false | Boolean or integer (nonzero is true). Default false; explicitly clears the saved enable. [READ] |
| `params.timelapse.delay_sec` | number | no | - | Frame delay, INFERRED seconds. Integer or float. Default is the saved value. Must be greater than 0 when timelapse is enabled (209 otherwise); no upper bound here. [READ] |
| `params.timelapse.src_dura_min` | integer | no | - | Source duration in minutes, unscaled; drives the worker stop in timelapse mode. Strict integer. Default is the saved value. No range check in the handler; downstream limits are unresolved. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 207 | The live image thread is not running, or an unspecified transitive failure | `fail to operate` |
| 524 | A planet stack is active locally, or the secondary unit reports the function busy | `function conflict` |
| 268 | The write thread is already running or an AVI file is already open | `operation is in progress` |
| 209 | Timelapse enabled with delay_sec not greater than 0 | `invalid value` |
| 208 | Not enough disk space | `disk is full` |
| 212 | The worker thread could not be created | `fail to create thread` |
| 300 | Relay to the secondary unit has no request context | `internal error` |
| 218 | AVI file creation failed (also reported by the AviRecord fail event) | `fail to write file` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

The complete set of relayed, crop-sync, disk and codec error codes is unresolved.

## Example

Request, plain:

```json
{"id":151,"method":"start_record_avi"}
```

Request, timelapse:

```json
{"id":152,"method":"start_record_avi","params":{"raw":false,"timelapse":{"enable":true,"delay_sec":5,"src_dura_min":30}}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_record_avi","result":0,"code":0,"id":151}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"start_record_avi","error":"function conflict","code":524,"id":153}
```
